title: Exact normalized quotient completion with its shift-compatible unit
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbb Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] let $B_T=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. In the derived category of $B_T$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $C_T$ and $\eta$ be exactly the normalized quotient-Roos completion and its augmentation of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], using restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and the strict mapping fibre [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then $C_T$ is additive and admits coherent integer shifts for which it is triangulated and $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to C_T$ commutes with shifts. The site and coefficient universes are independent. No completeness assertion about any object is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: Use the additive quotient Roos functor on the homotopy category, with coherent exact shifts and the normalized zero-second-coordinate augmentation. This is the purely homotopy-level part; it requires neither K-flat resolutions nor a derived completion.

proof.text: For the resolving class take homotopy classes represented by K-flat complexes whose terms are flat on the site. K-flat resolutions give a quasi-isomorphism from such an object to every homotopy object. Convert tensor flatness to site flatness with siteSheafTensorRightIso. Fullness of the homotopy quotient and the already proved roosGoodInverts show that the native homotopy functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms between these representatives. Apply leftDerived_from_resolvingClass.

source.place: Tags 06XN and 05SE, resolving-class derived functors; Tags 014E, 011G and 08TC for the native quotient Roos functor.

proof.text: Use rightKanExtension_coherentShift to choose the derived shifts whose counit commutes with shifts. Quasi-isomorphisms form a saturated triangulated multiplicative system. Resolving-class essential constancy supplies derived definedness everywhere. leftDerived_kan_map_source_distinguished proves source-triangle exactness for precisely these shifts; localization of arrows and isTriangulated_of_precomp give derived exactness.

proof.text: On good complexes, compose the derived counit with the native comparison. The counit is invertible there. completion_exists uniquely identifies the derived functor with the specified completion; transport shifts and exactness along this isomorphism. Additivity follows from exactness.

source.place: Tags 06XN and 05SE, resolving-class derived functors; Tags 014E, 011G and 08TC for the native quotient Roos functor.

proof.text: Lift the native augmentation from the identity through the right Kan extension. To prove shift compatibility, postcompose both candidate shift equations with the shifted counit. Postcomposition by a shift equivalence preserves the Kan property; its uniqueness detects equality. Naturality, the counit shift equation, and native augmentation compatibility prove the equality. Finally completionUnit_existsUnique identifies the transported lift with completionUnit by its prescribed normalization on good complexes.

lean.statement:
theorem integralQuotientCompletion_exact
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t}) [CompactSpace T] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T]
    (_hl : ∀ x : T, IsUnit (l : T.residueField x)) :
    (completion l E T none).Additive ∧
      ∃ (_ : (completion l E T none).CommShift ℤ),
        (completion l E T none).IsTriangulated ∧
          NatTrans.CommShift (completionUnit l E T none) ℤ
